citation: Panjabi MM, Goel V, Oxland T, Takata K, Duranceau J, Krag M, Price M. Human Lumbar Vertebrae: Quantitative Three-Dimensional Anatomy. Spine 1992;17(3):299-306. Copy read: bordercall archive/bordercall/reference/papers/Panjabi_1992_Lumbar_Spine_17-3_299-306.pdf, sha256 begins 842736d7102c0327; an 8-page scan with no text layer, journal pp. 299-306 = PDF pp. 1-8. Methods referred to ref 13 (Panjabi, Takata, Goel et al., Thoracic human vertebrae, Spine 16:888-901, 1991), used here only where labelled.
population: 12 fresh autopsy spines, C2 (axis) to the last lumbar vertebra, no sacrum; this report 60 lumbar vertebrae (L1-L5 of the 12 spines; Inference: 12 x 5). 8 men and 4 women (male/female 8/4), age mean 46.3 y (19-59), weight mean 67.8 kg (54-85), height mean 167.8 cm (157-178). Country and ethnicity not stated (Inference: United States, Yale affiliation). Radiographed to identify significant abnormalities; none reported, no exclusions reported. Same 12 donors as ref 13 (Inference): ref 13 Table 1 (p. 889) gives 5 carcinomas, 3 cardiac deaths, 1 each leukaemia, renal failure, burns, subdural haemorrhage; heaviest 84 kg. p. 299 (PDF 1); p. 300 (PDF 2).
modality: Dry-bone 3D morphometry: soft tissue removed (ref 13 p. 888: boiled, bleach 0.5 h, 75% ethanol 1 h); two threaded marker rods per body (printed 2 mm diameter, 2.5 mm long; ref 13 says 3.0 mm by 3.2 cm); a three-transducer morphometer (one LVDT, two RVDT, spherical coordinates) touched each point and the three markers; parts digitized as point loops (end plates, pedicles, processes) or spanning point sets (facets, up to 20 points); vertebral frame from a least-squares plane on four posterior-wall corner points, origin at the upper end-plate centre (ref 13 p. 889: X to the left along the upper corners). Linear, angular (plane fits) and area (Euclidean sum of three projected areas) parameters; mean +/- SEM of 12; one-way ANOVA with Scheffe at 95%. Accuracy under 5% on a Plexiglas phantom (30, 45, 60 deg faces); point error +/-0.5 mm in ref 13 (p. 889). No radiographic or CT measurement. pp. 299-300 (PDF 1-2).
levels_covered: L1 to L5 only (sacrum not kept). Numbering method not stated; Inference: every spine numbered as 5 lumbar (60 = 12 x 5) and, in ref 13, 12 thoracic (144 = 12 x 12); no transitional or numerical variant reported.

anomalies.variant: Lumbosacral transitional vertebra, sacralisation, lumbarisation, L6, T13, rib-count variants, block vertebrae
anomalies.finding: None reported. Every spine contributes five lumbar levels (60 vertebrae of 12 spines, arithmetic); the sacrum was not kept, so a partially sacralised L5 could not be seen on the specimen; the screening radiographs' findings are not given. Inference: even as 0 of 12, the one-sided 95% upper bound is about 22%, so no prior can be drawn.
anomalies.population: 12 fresh autopsy spines, 8 men and 4 women, 19-59 y
anomalies.how_identified: Specimens radiographed (projection not stated) to identify any significant abnormalities; no result reported.

anomalies.finding: Abstract calls L1-L2 transitional toward the thoracic region and L4-L5 toward the sacral region; the discussion divides the lumbar spine into a thoracolumbar transition (canal depth narrowing L1-L3, pedicle height falling), a middle region at L3 (narrow canal, greatest end-plate areas, longest SPL) and a lumbosacral transition (canal area enlarging L3-L5, pedicles enlarging, PDIs +8 deg at L5). These are normal regional shapes, not LSTV prevalence.
anomalies.how_identified: Trends of the measured means across levels.

measures.name: Vertebral body frame (reference for all measures)
measures.definition: Least-squares plane through four digitized posterior-wall points (left and right, upper and lower edges) = frontal plane xy; transverse xz and sagittal yz planes follow; origin = digitized centre of the upper end plate. Figure 1: Y cranial, Z anterior, X lateral. Ref 13 p. 889: Z normal to the frontal plane, X parallel to the line through the two superior corners pointing to the left, Y perpendicular to the z-x plane, origin the centroid of the superior end plate; corners chosen as least affected by osteophytes.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: locate the four posterior-wall corners of the body, fit a plane, Z = normal toward the body, X = right-to-left direction through the upper corners projected into the plane, Y = Z x X, origin = superior end-plate centroid; rotate the mask into this frame before every extent.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: true lateral gives Y along the posterior body line and Z perpendicular; AP cannot separate posterior from anterior corners; rotation breaks the frame.

measures.name: EPWu, EPWl: upper and lower end-plate width
measures.definition: Lateral width of the end-plate loop along X; Figure 1 front view spans the rim to the lateral lips.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: X extent of the cranial (caudal) body surface rim in the posterior-wall frame, lipping included; SPINEPS 52/53.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP view, end-plate line between lateral cortices over magnification; not from a lateral.
measures.level_pattern: Rises about 14% L1 to L5 (EPWu 41.2 to 47.3; EPWl 43.3 to 49.5 at L4, 49.4 at L5); lower exceeds upper by 2.1-3.9 mm at every level; only L4 and L5 differ from L1; no adjacent pair separated.
measures.covariates: Pooled; no sex, age or size breakdown.
measures.error: SEM 0.74-1.41 mm (SD about 2.6-4.9 mm, computed); method under 5%.

measures.name: EPDu, EPDl: upper and lower end-plate depth
measures.definition: Anteroposterior depth of the end-plate loop along Z, anterior rim to posterior rim (Figure 1 side view).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: Z extent of the end-plate rim in the posterior-wall frame.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral view end-plate line over magnification; not from AP.
measures.level_pattern: Relatively constant (EPDu 34.1-35.5; EPDl 35.3 at L1 to 33.2 at L5); no significant difference; does not separate levels.

measures.name: EPW/EPD ratios, upper and lower (derived)
measures.definition: Width over depth; printed values are ratios of the group means (computed check).
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: ratio of the two mask extents, averaged as a ratio of means.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP width over lateral depth.
measures.level_pattern: Upper 1.21, 1.23, 1.25, 1.31, 1.36 (about +12%); lower 1.23, 1.30, 1.38, 1.46, 1.49 (+21%); the lower ratio is the most regular body gradient.

measures.name: EPAu, EPAl: end-plate area
measures.definition: Projected areas of the end-plate loop on xy, yz and zx; total = square root of the sum of their squares. Inference: the magnitude of the loop's vector area, i.e. the area enclosed by the rim, not the concave surface.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: area enclosed by the rim, projected on the end plate's best-fit plane.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Not measurable; pi x EPW x EPD / 4 overestimates by under 10% (p. 305, PDF 7; computed 1.7-7.5%).
measures.level_pattern: L5 17% (upper) and 9% (lower) above L1; upper rises nearly linearly L1-L4 (1057 to 1239) and holds; lower peaks at L3 (1290); no significant difference.

measures.name: EPItu, EPItl: end-plate inclination to the transverse plane
measures.definition: Angle between the least-squares plane of the end-plate points and the vertebra's transverse plane. Inference: unsigned, combines sagittal and coronal tilt; no sagittal- or frontal-plane end-plate angle tabulated.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: angle between the end-plate surface plane normal and the vertebra's Y axis.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral gives the sagittal component only.
measures.level_pattern: EPItu 1.7-4.7 deg, EPItl 1.8-4.0 deg, no trend, no significant difference; no level information.
measures.error: Phantom tested at 30-60 deg only; Inference: relative error says little at 2-5 deg.

measures.name: VBHp: posterior vertebral body height
measures.definition: Body height at the posterior wall between the end plates (Figure 1 side view, vertical double arrow); suffix a (anterior) defined but no anterior height reported.
measures.page: Fig 1 p. 300 (PDF 2); Table 1 and 2 p. 301 (PDF 3); p. 304 (PDF 6)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: Y extent of the body in a thin posterior slab, not the maximum height; midline or corner mean not stated (SPINEPS_MAPPING.md: median column height in the posterior 20% of label 49).
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral, posterior wall height over magnification.
measures.level_pattern: Flat L1-L4 (23.8, 24.3, 23.8, 24.1), lowest at L5 (22.9); no significant difference.
measures.error: SEM 0.95-1.10 mm. Close to Cotterill; text says 1-2 mm below Berry, Scoles, Gilad, but Table 6 shows 3-5 mm below Scoles and Gilad.

measures.name: SCW: spinal canal width
measures.definition: Lateral width of the canal; Figure 1 top view draws a transverse double arrow across the canal near mid-depth (Inference: at the pedicles); level within the canal not stated.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: X extent of the bony vertebral foramen in the vertebra's transverse plane at the pedicles; not SPINEPS label 61 (canal contents).
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP interpedicular distance over magnification.
measures.level_pattern: Increases steadily 23.7 (L1) to 27.1 (L5), nearly flat L1-L3, faster L3-L5; no significant difference.

measures.name: SCD: spinal canal depth
measures.definition: Anteroposterior depth in the midline from the posterior body wall to the anterior surface of the arch at the spinous base (Figure 1 top view).
measures.page: p. 301 (PDF 3); Fig 1 p. 300 (PDF 2); Table 3 p. 302 (PDF 4); p. 304 (PDF 6)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: Z extent of the foramen in the midsagittal plane.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: lateral, posterior body line to spinolaminar line over magnification.
measures.level_pattern: Parabola: 19.0, 18.2, 17.5, 18.6, 19.7; minimum at L3; rises T10-T12 above (ref 13 via p. 304); no significant difference.

measures.name: SCW/SCD: canal width to depth (derived)
measures.page: Table 3 p. 302 (PDF 4); p. 301 (PDF 3); Fig 3B p. 303 (PDF 5); p. 304 (PDF 6)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: ratio of the two foramen extents.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP width over lateral depth.
measures.level_pattern: 1.25, 1.31, 1.39, 1.37, 1.38: rises L1-L3, then constant; marks the upper transition zone.

measures.name: SCA: spinal canal area
measures.definition: Cross-sectional area by the projected-area method; digitizing of the canal not described.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: area of the closed bony foramen in the transverse plane at the pedicles.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Not measurable; ellipse from SCW and SCD overestimates 10-30%, triangle underestimates 20-30%; ellipse better above, triangle below.
measures.level_pattern: 320, 281, 280, 290, 330: falls L1-L2, constant L2-L4, enlarges L3-L5 (lumbosacral transition).

measures.name: PDW, PDH (right, left): pedicle width and height
measures.definition: Cross-sectional width and height of the circumferential pedicle loop; where along the pedicle is not stated, nor that it was the narrowest section.
measures.page: p. 299 (PDF 1); p. 301 (PDF 3); Fig 1 p. 300 (PDF 2); Table 4 p. 302 (PDF 4)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: SPINEPS has no pedicle label; take the narrowest section between body and arch; X extent = PDW, Y extent = PDH.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP pedicle oval (distorted by 14-25 deg convergence); lateral gives PDH with sides superimposed.
measures.level_pattern: PDH 15.9 (L1), 14.4 (L3), 19.6 (L5); PDW 8.6 (L1), 8.2 (L2), then about +3.5 mm per level to 18.6 (L5; text 18.9). L4 PDW differs from L1-L2 (r) and L1-L3 (l); every L5 PDW and PDH differs from L1-L4.
measures.error: SEM 0.46-1.03 mm, except PDWr L4 0.18 mm.

measures.name: PDH/PDW (right, left): pedicle height to width (derived)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: ratio of the section's Y and X extents.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: AP oval height over width.

measures.name: PDA (right, left): pedicle cross-sectional area
measures.definition: Projected-area method on the pedicle loop.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: area of the narrowest section between body and arch.
measures.level_pattern: Falls L1-L2 (86.4/88.5 to 83.3/83.6), rises to 143.9/158.7 at L5; ellipse best at L1-L2, triangle at L4-L5; computed: L5 area below even PDW x PDH / 2.

measures.name: PDIs, PDIt (right, left): pedicle inclination
measures.definition: Angle of the pedicle centre line (perpendicular to its section) to the vertebra's sagittal (PDIs) and transverse (PDIt) planes; Figure 1: convergent anteromedially, posterior end higher. Inference: unsigned.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: normal of the narrowest pedicle section; angles to the vertebra's yz and xz planes.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: PDIs needs an axial image; PDIt approximated on a lateral.
measures.level_pattern: PDIs about 14.5 (L1), lowest 14.1 (L2), 18.5 (L3) above 16.0-16.6 (L4), 24.6 (L5, +8 deg over L4); only PDIsl L5 vs L1-L2 significant. PDIt 2.5 to 5.5 deg.
measures.error: SEM 0.64-3.75 deg, PDIsr L1 5.02 deg (SD about 17 deg).

measures.name: PDMs, PDMt: pedicle second moments of area (derived)
measures.definition: Ellipse formulas from PDH and PDW: pi x PDH^3 x PDW / 64 (sagittal) and pi x PDH x PDW^3 / 64 (transverse, printed PDM).
measures.level_pattern: Constant L1-L3, sharp rise to L5; sagittal always above transverse.

measures.name: PIA (right, left): pars interarticularis area
measures.definition: Cross-sectional area of the pars; no landmark, plane or digitizing rule given.
measures.page: Table 1 p. 301 (PDF 3); p. 302 (PDF 4); Table 5 and Fig 5 p. 304 (PDF 6)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: narrowest pars section within SPINEPS arch label 41, each side.
measures.level_pattern: Gradual increase, about 62 (L1) to 81 (L5) by the text; table L5 92.9 r, 71.7 l; only PIAr L5 vs L1 significant; Figure 5 plots PIAr L3 at 80 where Table 5 prints 70.0.
measures.error: SEM 1.17-9.76 mm2, L1 far smaller than the rest.

measures.name: SPL: spinous process length
measures.definition: From the centre of the superior end plate (origin) to the most inferoposterior tip of the spinous process; the whole vertebra's reach, not the process alone.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: 3D distance from the superior end-plate centroid to the farthest posteroinferior voxel of SPINEPS label 42 (Inference for the voxel rule).
measures.radiograph_recipe: Inference: true lateral, both points midsagittal, over magnification.
measures.level_pattern: 67.7, 71.7, 71.7, 70.1, 68.3: greatest L2-L3, tied by the authors to the lordotic apex at L3; no significant difference.

measures.name: TPW: transverse process width
measures.definition: Distance from the tip of the left transverse process to the tip of the right.
measures.page: p. 302 (PDF 4); Fig 1 p. 300 (PDF 2); Table 5 and Fig 6 p. 304 (PDF 6)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: 3D distance between the most lateral voxels of SPINEPS 43 and 44.
measures.level_pattern: 71.2, 76.1, 85.7, 79.4, 92.5: local peak at L3 (vs L1 only significant), L5 differs from L1, L2 and L4.
measures.error: SEM 1.48-3.78 mm, largest at L4-L5 (SD about 13 mm).

level_details.detail: Canal depth narrows L1-L3 while width stays nearly constant, against its rise T10-T12; width/depth ratio rises L1-L3; pedicle height falls slightly L1-L3, continuing T11-T12; pedicle widths only 8-9 mm.
Narrowest end plates (EPWu 41.2, EPWl 43.3), smallest TPW (71.2), second-deepest canal (19.0), tallest-narrowest pedicles (PDH/PDW 2.00 r, 1.72 l), smallest pars area.
Smallest pedicle width (8.2 mm by the text), area (83 mm2) and convergence (PDIs 14.1); canal area 281 with L3 the smallest.

Middle region: narrowest canal depth (17.5) and area (280), largest lower end-plate area (1290), longest SPL with L2 (71.7), lowest pedicle height (14.4), local peaks of TPW (85.7) and PDIs; authors tie it to the lordotic apex.
Widest lower end plate (49.5), deepest upper end plate (35.5), largest upper end-plate area (1239); pedicle width jumps to 14.1; PDWl separates L3 from L4 (the only significant L3/L4 difference).

Canal area enlarges L3-L5; pedicles grow sharply L3-L5 (attributed to larger loads, supported by moments of inertia); PDIs 8 deg above L4, the fanning toward the sacrum; lowest VBHp (22.9), shallowest lower end plate (33.2), widest canal (27.1), largest canal area (330), widest TPW (92.5), near-round pedicles about 19 mm. L4/L5 separated by PDW, PDH, PDAl and TPW. Sacrum not studied.
Only L3/L4 (PDWl) and L4/L5 (PDW, PDH, PDAl, TPW) are separated at P < .05; nothing separates L1/L2 or L2/L3.

errors.what: Accuracy of linear, angular and area parameters on a Plexiglas phantom with graph-paper shapes on 30, 45 and 60 deg faces
Largest instrument error locating a point (ref 13, same series)

errors.value: SEM of 12 specimens; SD = SEM x sqrt(12), about 3.46 x SEM (computed)

errors.what: Observer repeatability, per-level n, landmark error
Odd dispersions (Inference: misprint or one deviant specimen)
errors.value: PDWr L4 SEM 0.18 mm; PDIsr L1 SEM 5.02 deg; TPW L4-L5 SEM 3.78 and 3.68 mm; PIA L1 SEM 1.17-2.19 mm2

pearls_pitfalls.text: Canal size relates to low-back pain incidence (ref 14) and is affected by childhood physiologic stresses (ref 2, infant malnutrition and adult stenosis).
The concavity of the posterior body wall in the horizontal plane has been postulated to affect the frequency of disc herniation (no reference).
Pedicle size and orientation govern transpedicular fixation design and surgery; instability, trauma, screw design, diagnosis, device design and predictive models are the named uses.

Upper lumbar pedicles are very narrow (8-9 mm) and taller than wide (1.84); lower ones are round, larger and more convergent (L5 about 8 deg more than L4). Inference: width limits screw diameter at L1-L2, a more medial path is needed at L5.
Pedicle bending stiffness is greater in the sagittal than the transverse plane at every level.
Pedicle section near-elliptical at L1-L2, near-triangular at L4-L5; canal better an ellipse above, a triangle below.
Pitfall: 'transitional' means a morphological zone, not an LSTV.
Pitfall: other series disagree at L4-L5 on pedicle height and width, on VBHp (3-5 mm higher in Scoles and Gilad) and on canal depth (Cotterill 12.1 at L3); compare only like definitions.
Pitfall (ref 13): build the frame on the posterior-wall corners, which vary least with osteophytes.
Not in the paper: stenosis thresholds, syndromes, sex differences, safe zones, screw sizes.

instructions.text: Build each vertebra's frame from the four posterior-wall corners (plane = frontal; Z toward the body; X through the upper corners toward the left; Y = Z x X; origin at the upper end-plate centre) and measure every width, depth and height along it, never along scanner axes.
Measure SPL as the 3D distance from the superior end-plate centre to the most inferoposterior spinous tip.
Measure SCD in the midline from the posterior body wall to the arch, SCW across the bony foramen (at the pedicles, Inference from Fig 1), never on the dural sac or at a disc level.
Expect SCD to bottom out at L3 and rise toward L1 and L5 (and T10-T12 above); use the turning point over several bodies, not one.
Use size-free ratios (lower EPW/EPD 1.23 to 1.49; PDH/PDW 1.84 at L1-L2 to 1.0 at L5; SCW/SCD 1.25 to 1.39 at L3 then flat) when size is unknown, computed as ratios of means.
Tell L4 from L5 by pedicle size (L5 about 19 mm wide and high, round) and TPW (L5 about 92 mm); use the 8 deg extra L5 convergence only as support, it is not significant.
Do not expect any single measure to separate L1/L2 or L2/L3; decide them on the sequence.
Treat TPW longer at L3 than L4 (85.7 vs 79.4) as a weak, non-significant hint.
Ignore end-plate inclination and VBHp for lumbar level naming, except VBHp's drop at L5.
Take end-plate area as the rim-enclosed area; from AP width and lateral depth, pi x W x D / 4 is within 10%.
Do not use the ellipse for canal area at L4-L5 (about 27-28% high, computed); use the triangle there.
Take the pedicle as the narrowest section between body and arch and record which section was used, since the paper does not say.
Never use this paper for anomaly prevalence; it reports none and kept no sacrum.
Compare with Panjabi using SD = SEM x sqrt(12) plus at least 5% method error.

On AP radiographs expect interpedicular distance to widen caudally (slowly L1-L3, faster L3-L5) and pedicle ovals to go from tall-narrow (L1-L2) to round (L4-L5); Inference that projection keeps both trends.
Remember the reference is boiled, bleached dry bone without discs or ligaments; expect small rim offsets against living CT (Inference).

bordercall: (a) Anomaly priors: none; 0 of 12 reported is uninformative (one-sided 95% upper bound about 22%, computed); priors must come from other papers.

(b) Generator already holds Tables 2-5. Add EPW/EPD, PDH/PDW, SCW/SCD as ratios of means; PDM adds nothing. Facets were digitized but not reported here; lumbar facets come from the 1993 facets paper of the series.

(b) SPL: paper starts at the superior end-plate centre (p. 302); mnemonics.py says posterior canal wall, the archive measurer the body centroid (SPINEPS_MAPPING.md); both differ from the lumbar definition.

(b) PDW/PDH/PDA: mnemonics.py says smallest diameters and area at the narrowest; paper says only cross-sectional loop; L5 areas (143.9, 158.7) are below PDW x PDH / 2 (176, 187), so the three do not describe one convex square-cut section.
(b) SCW 'at the level of the pedicles' in mnemonics.py is not stated in the paper; SPINEPS label 61 is canal contents, not the bony foramen.
(b) EPA is the rim-enclosed (vector) area; a mesh surface area reads high. Angles are unsigned magnitudes to the vertebra's own planes.
(b) Extents must be taken in the posterior-wall frame (X to the left, ref 13 p. 889), not scanner axes, or EPD and VBHp inflate at L4-L5.
(b) PIAr L3: Figure 5 plots 80 against Table 5's 70.0 (Inference: table misprint); do not lean on PIA.
(b) SPINEPS_MAPPING.md calls the specimens 'embalmed'; the paper says fresh autopsy, cleaned by boiling, bleach and ethanol (ref 13 p. 888).
(c) Error: method under 5% (p. 300); point error +/-0.5 mm (ref 13 p. 889); bordercall's 1 mm, 3 deg and sqrt(pi A / 2) x 1 mm fit short lengths but understate 5% for SPL and TPW (3.4-4.6 mm).

(d) Covariates: 8 M, 4 F, 19-59 y, 54-85 kg, 157-178 cm; no breakdown by sex, age or size, no population named; per-specimen demographics exist in ref 13 but no per-specimen measures, so no size regression.
gaps: Figure 5 plots PIAr L3 at 80 (and PIAavg about 77.5) where Table 5 prints 70.0; other pars points match within 0.5 mm2; text's gradual increase fits 80 (new; not in CONTRADICTIONS.md).
Text vs table: PDW L5 18.9 (p. 301) vs 18.6 mean; PIA L5 81 (p. 302) vs 82.3 mean (both in CONTRADICTIONS.md).
Table 6 PDIs L4 16.0 vs Table 4 mean 16.55 (in CONTRADICTIONS.md).
Weight range 54-85 kg vs ref 13 Table 1 maximum 84 kg (in CONTRADICTIONS.md).
Marker rods printed 2 mm by 2.5 mm long (p. 299) vs 3.0 mm by 3.2 cm in ref 13 (p. 888); 2.5 mm is implausible.
Upper-zone sentence contrasts 8-9 mm pedicle widths with '15-16 mm heights at the lower lumbar levels' (p. 304); those heights belong to the upper levels.
SPL and TPW cited to Table 6 (p. 302) but are in Table 5.
SCD called the narrowest portion 'in the lateral dimension' (p. 301).
Figure 2C ellipse curve called dotted in the text (p. 301), dashed in the caption (p. 303).
VBHp '1-2 mm' below others (p. 304) is 3-5 mm vs Scoles and Gilad in Table 6; pedicle-angle 'remarkable consistency' and SCW 'extremely well' are not borne out at every level of Table 6.
Pedicle ellipse said best at L1-L2 (p. 305); computed, only on the right side; triangle closer on the left at L1.
Abstract assigns zones to L1-L2 and L4-L5, discussion describes L1-L3 and L3-L5.

Unstated: how L1 was identified; screening radiograph findings; per-level n; canal and pars digitizing; where along the pedicle; +X side (given only in ref 13); sign conventions; observer repeatability; anterior body height; sacral data; facet results.
Inference: compare Panjabi's L3 SCD minimum with skeletal and radiographic series (e.g. Eisenstein) only by matching definitions.
